intro: An accessibility team must audit the {n} archived pages {first} to {last} against the rulebook that follows and report the offending elements of every page, rule by rule. The pages are static HTML from an offline web archive of real encyclopedia and software-documentation pages with some edited parts, and they are only available through the tools; there are no stylesheets or scripts, only the HTML and its inline style attributes.
rule_scope: Every img, input, select, textarea, button, a, h1-h6 and table element in a page carries an attribute data-ref="r<number>" that is unique within one page, and offenders are reported by these data-ref values; only the duplicate-id rule reports ids instead. Refs are only unique within one page, so the same ref can name different elements on different pages. Definitions used by all rules: an element's text is its text content with whitespace collapsed, including the alt attribute of any img inside it and excluding the content of hidden descendants; a value is blank when it is empty after collapsing whitespace.
rule_hidden: An element is hidden when it or any of its ancestors has the hidden attribute, aria-hidden="true", or an inline style that declares display: none or visibility: hidden; aria-hidden="false" hides nothing. Hidden elements are exempt from the image, form-control, link/button, heading and table rules, and hidden headings are skipped in the heading sequence. Text referenced through aria-labelledby counts even when the referenced element is hidden. The duplicate-id rule covers every element, hidden or not.
rule_img: Answer key img_alt. A visible img offends unless it has at least one of: an alt attribute (any value, including an empty alt=""), role="presentation" or role="none", a non-blank aria-label, an aria-labelledby whose listed ids include at least one id that exists on the page and the referenced text is non-blank, or a non-blank title. An img also offends when its alt is just a file name: only letters, digits, spaces, underscores, hyphens and dots, ending in .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif, .svg or .webp in any letter case.
rule_control: Answer key control_name. Visible input, select and textarea elements need an accessible name; input elements of type hidden, submit or reset are exempt, and an input without a type attribute is a text input. A control has a name when any of these holds: a non-blank aria-label; an aria-labelledby whose referenced text is non-blank, where ids that do not exist contribute nothing; a label element anywhere on the page whose for attribute equals the control's id, with non-blank text, where a for attribute only labels the first element on the page that carries that id; an enclosing label element that has no for attribute, whose text not counting the content of form controls inside it is non-blank; a non-blank title; for type="button" a non-blank value; for type="image" a non-blank alt. A placeholder never counts as a name.
rule_link: Answer key link_name. This rule covers visible a elements that have an href attribute and visible button elements; a elements without href are exempt. The name is the first non-blank of: the aria-label; the text referenced by aria-labelledby; the element's own text; the title. The element offends when the name is blank, or when the name, lowercased and with spaces and the characters . , : ; ! ? … » › > → removed from both ends, equals one of these generic phrases: {generic}.
rule_heading: Answer key heading_skip. Go through the visible h1-h6 elements in document order, starting from level 0. A heading offends when its level is more than one greater than the level of the previous visible heading, so the first visible heading offends unless it is an h1. Every visible heading, offending or not, becomes the previous heading for the next one. Moving to a lower level by any amount is allowed.
rule_dup: Answer key duplicate_id. Report every id value that appears on two or more elements of the page, hidden or not, comparing values exactly, so letter case matters. Report the id values themselves, not data-ref values.
rule_lang: Answer key lang_ok. The value is true when the html element has a lang attribute whose value is two or three ASCII letters, optionally followed by subtags that are each a hyphen plus one to eight ASCII letters or digits (for example en, en-GB, fr); only the form of the value is checked, not whether it matches the page language. A missing, empty or malformed lang gives false.
rule_table: Answer key table_header. A visible table that does not have role="presentation" or role="none" offends when it contains no th cell of its own; th cells inside a nested table belong to that nested table only.
answer_line: The final answer is one JSON object that maps every page id to an object with exactly these seven keys: img_alt, control_name, link_name, heading_skip and table_header (lists of data-ref values in any order), duplicate_id (a list of id values) and lang_ok (true or false); use an empty list when a rule has no offenders. A page counts only when all seven entries are exactly right. Format example: {example}.
unit_prompt: Audit only page {page} with the tools and the rulebook that follows, and finish with one JSON object that contains only that page, in the format of {example}.

tools.list_pages: Lists the page ids, titles and line counts of the archived pages; takes optional offset and limit parameters.
tools.read_page: Returns numbered lines of one page starting at start_line, about 7,400 characters per call, and tells the next start_line.
tools.search_page: Lists the lines of one page that contain a given text, case-insensitive, with line numbers; returns at most 40 lines, each cut to 300 characters.
